title: Demand Service Rate Programs: What the Program Year's Emergency Dispatches Add to a Settlement
content:
Where the emergency dispatches counted against the current program year stand at more than twice the
tier's included emergency calls, the tier's emergency call surcharge taken at 1.5 is taken in for each
dispatch beyond the included calls. Where those dispatches stand above the tier's included emergency
calls but not above twice them, the tier's emergency call surcharge is taken in for each dispatch beyond
the included calls. Where they stand at or below the included calls, nothing is taken in for emergency
dispatches.

The two program figures the terms turn on, under the Demand Service Rate Programs:

| Program | Emergency dispatches included per program year | Emergency call surcharge (USD per dispatch) |
|---|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 0 | 350 |
| Priority Response Program | 1 | 295 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 2 | 250 |
| Emergency Response Program | 6 | 195 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 12 | 150 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 24 | 0 |

| Dispatches counted against the current program year | Taken in for each dispatch beyond the included calls |
|---|---|
| more than twice the included calls | the tier's emergency call surcharge taken at 1.5 |
| above the included calls, not above twice them | the tier's emergency call surcharge |
| at or below the included calls | nothing is taken in |

**Both sides of the counts (hypothetical).** On the Block Hour Service Program, which includes 2
emergency dispatches and carries a surcharge of 250 US dollars: 4 dispatches counted in the program year
stand above the included calls but not above twice them, so 250 US dollars is taken in for each of the 2
dispatches beyond the included calls; 5 dispatches stand at more than twice the included calls, so 375
US dollars is taken in for each of the 3 beyond them; 2 dispatches leave nothing to be taken in.
